messages.author: d0b18666fe8582cb
messages.subject: fixed calibration
parts:
Hi there,

I'm wondering if anyone could point me to guidance on using mirt for fixed calibration? I ran a unidimensional graded response model on a 6 item scale (x1-x6).  Item x6, however, was showing LD with items x2 and x5, so I removed x6 from the scale and calibrated only the 5 item scale (x1-x5). But I'd like to still obtain item parameter estimates for the 6th item (on the metric of the 5-item calibration without the influence of LD), so I was planning perform a fixed parameter calibration, where I calibrate x6 onto the metric of x1,x3, and x4, with the item parameter estimates of x1,x3, and x4 fixed at their previously estimated values (from calibration with items x1-x5).  I found this post, but i'm not sure this is the right approach for my situation: https://groups.google.com/forum/#!searchin/mirt-package/item$20parameters$20as$20fixed%7Csort:date/mirt-package/QZbzozxO9H0/UVjUGXoOBAAJ . Normally, I would just get rid of the LD item, but I'm trying to describe the properties of an existing scale using IRT vs. developing a new scale, so I'm still interested in obtaining item parameter estimates for the offending x6 item.

Any suggestions are appreciated! Thank you,

Keri

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: fixed calibration
parts:
It's not possible to edit the rows of the object irt11.params here, only its respective elements. So, if you need something like the $values changed you have to replace those explicitly, not just take a subset of some other objects. In other words, these should be the same before and after editing:

dim(irt11.params)
sapply(irt11.params, class)

HTH. 

Phil

messages.subject: Re: fixed calibration
parts:
How has your data been collected? For example, do you have the same individuals who answered items in both calibration 1 and 2? Or Is calibration 1 one sample, while calibration 2 is a completely different sample? The reason I'm asking has to do with how you should be organizing the data to so such linking (the latter is going to require a lot of sparse NA placeholders, and the linking would have to be taken purely on faith if the calibration samples do not contain common items). 

Phil

parts:
The setup of this seems kind of weird for me conceptually, in that I'm not sure why you aren't just estimating the new item at the same time as the first calibration set (which would incidentally improve their parameter estimates as well), but I'll play along. 

A few more questions. In calibration 2, does this dataset also have items 1,2, and 4? In other words, did the respondents see the same items twice. What I'm trying to do is simulate some data for us to work with so that I can see your setup, but so far it's not quite clear to me yet.

library(mirt)
a <- rlnorm(6)
d <- rnorm(6)
dat <- simdata(a, d, 1000, itemtype = '2PL')

dat1 <- dat[,1:5] # first calibration set of items
dat2 <- dat[,6, drop=FALSE] # item 6 by itself in calibration 2?

Phil

parts:
Hi Phil, thanks so much for your wisdom! 

Yes the second calibration (step 3 below) would have items 1,2, and 4. The data are cross-sectional and all respondents only saw each item once. This could be conceptually weird because maybe it is not the best approach....?

I'm only doing another calibration because in the initial calibration item x6 showed local dependence with items x3 and x5; so I removed item 6 and recalibrated items 1-5. But because I'm evaluating the psychometric properties of an existing scale, I still want to obtain item parameter estimates for the offending LD item (x6) (if possible, but without biasing the other item parameter estimates). So my thought was to calibrate x6 onto the metric of the calibration where only x1-x5 were included. Then in this separate calibration I would fix items x1, x2 and x4 their previously calibrated values. My logic for doing this is to obtain item parameter estimates for x6 (since x6 was not included in calibration 1). Since x6 is showing LD w/ x3 and x5 I was planned to not include them in the fixed calibration. 

Synthesis of my steps:
1. Calibrated 6 item scale using unidimensional GRM--> item 6 showing large LD w/ items 3 and 5; item 6 removed 
2. Re-calibrated 5 item scale using unidimensional GRM--> items 1-5 included; item 6 removed due to LD ("final calibration")
3. Fixed calibration using unidimensional GRM --> want to calibrate item 6 onto metric of calibration in step 2 with items fixed at values from step 2. Items 3 and 5 removed given they show LD w/ item 6. Only items 1,2,4 + 6 included.

thanks again, Phil.

Keri

The setup of this seems kind of weird for me conceptually, in that I'm not sure why you aren't just estimating the new item at the same time as the first calibration set (which would incidentally improve their parameter estimates as well), but I'll play along. 

A few more questions. In calibration 2, does this dataset also have items 1,2, and 4? In other words, did the respondents see the same items twice. What I'm trying to do is simulate some data for us to work with so that I can see your setup, but so far it's not quite clear to me yet.

library(mirt)
a <- rlnorm(6)
d <- rnorm(6)
dat <- simdata(a, d, 1000, itemtype = '2PL')

dat1 <- dat[,1:5] # first calibration set of items
dat2 <- dat[,6, drop=FALSE] # item 6 by itself in calibration 2?

How has your data been collected? For example, do you have the same individuals who answered items in both calibration 1 and 2? The reason I'm asking has to do with how you should be organizing the data to so such linking (the latter is going to require a lot of sparse NA placeholders, and the linking would have to be taken purely on faith if the calibration samples do not contain common items). 

Phil

I guess I'm still confused on how one would can calibrate a new item onto the metric of previously calibrated subset of items when the new item was not in the original calibration. 

In calibration 1, I calibrated items x1-x5. Now, in Calibration 2, I want to calibrate item x6 onto metric from Calibration 1, but with items x3 and x5 removed. I'm not sure how to do this without modifying the rows of the object created by pars = "values" function within mirt.

Tried to find guidance on there in the forum and outside of the forum but can't find anything that relates to this.. any wisdom is appreciated. thank you,

On Fri, Feb 15, 2019 at 9:22 PM Phil Chalmers <rphilip....@gmail.com> wrote:
It's not possible to edit the rows of the object irt11.params here, only its respective elements. So, if you need something like the $values changed you have to replace those explicitly, not just take a subset of some other objects. In other words, these should be the same before and after editing:

dim(irt11.params)
sapply(irt11.params, class)

HTH. 

Phil

I'm wondering if anyone could point me to guidance on using mirt for fixed calibration? I ran a unidimensional graded response model on a 6 item scale (x1-x6).  Item x6, however, was showing LD with items x2 and x5, so I removed x6 from the scale and calibrated only the 5 item scale (x1-x5). But I'd like to still obtain item parameter estimates for the 6th item (on the metric of the 5-item calibration without the influence of LD), so I was planning perform a fixed parameter calibration, where I calibrate x6 onto the metric of x1,x3, and x4, with the item parameter estimates of x1,x3, and x4 fixed at their previously estimated values (from calibration with items x1-x5).  I found this post, but i'm not sure this is the right approach for my situation: https://groups.google.com/forum/#!searchin/mirt-package/item$20parameters$20as$20fixed%7Csort:date/mirt-package/QZbzozxO9H0/UVjUGXoOBAAJ . Any suggestions are appreciated! Thank you,

Keri
